# Gilbert Blythe & Una Meredith

- [Gilbert Blythe](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) — Saved — [Una Meredith](../character/una-meredith.md) — since v5  <sub>[v5 CHAPTER XXVIII. A FAST DAY P16](../source/v05-c28.md#nw-v05-c28-p0016)</sub>

## Shared scenes

> At the church service, [Faith](../character/faith.md) addresses the congregation to clear her father's name regarding the house-cleaning incident, explaining the mix-up in days. The following day, [Faith](../character/faith.md) dares [Walter](../character/walter.md) to ride pigs through the village streets, drawing various reactions from the villagers. Later, Miss Cornelia visits [Ingleside](../codex/places.md#ingleside) to discuss Faith's antics with [Anne](../character/anne.md) and [Susan](../character/susan.md), leading to a lighthearted conversation about childhood and local town gossip.
>
> — v5 · CHAPTER XII. AN EXPLANATION AND A DARE

> [Cornelia Bryant](../character/cornelia-bryant.md) and [Susan](../character/susan.md) complain to [Anne](../character/anne.md) and [Gilbert](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) about the minister's children singing a lighthearted song in the graveyard during a [Methodist](../codex/factions.md#methodist) prayer meeting. After [Cornelia](../character/cornelia-bryant.md) brings the issue to Mr. Meredith's attention, he calls [Jerry](../character/jerry.md), [Faith](../character/faith.md), [Una](../character/una-meredith.md), and [Carl](../character/carl.md) into his study to gently reprimand them. Ashamed, the children resolve to punish themselves through their [Conduct Club](../codex/factions.md#conduct-club), while Mr. Meredith despairs over his parenting and longs for [Rosemary](../character/rosemary-west.md).
>
> — v5 · CHAPTER XXVII. A SACRED CONCERT

> [The Meredith](../codex/factions.md#the-meredith) children decide to fast all day Sunday as a self-imposed punishment for their Good-[Conduct Club](../codex/factions.md#conduct-club), but [Una](../character/una-meredith.md) faints during the evening church service from lack of food. Doctor [Gilbert Blythe](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) revives [Una](../character/una-meredith.md), and [Faith](../character/faith.md) explains to her father and Mrs. Clow that the children are raising themselves. Distressed by Faith's words, [John Meredith](../character/john-meredith.md) resolves to be a better father to his children, though he realizes he can never marry anyone but [Rosemary West](../character/rosemary-west.md).
>
> — v5 · CHAPTER XXVIII. A FAST DAY

> [Faith](../character/faith.md), [Carl](../character/carl.md), and [Una](../character/una-meredith.md) become terrified in [Rainbow Valley](../codex/places.md#rainbow-valley) when they mistake Mrs. [Stimson](../character/stimson.md)—who is crawling on the [Bailey](../codex/places.md#bailey) garden dyke with white sheets on her shoulders looking for a knitting needle—for the ghost of [Henry Warren](../character/henry-warren.md). Terrified, the Meredith children sprint to [Ingleside](../codex/places.md#ingleside), where [Rosemary West](../character/rosemary-west.md) and [Susan Baker](../character/susan.md) soothe them. [Susan](../character/susan.md) investigates with a pitchfork and returns to explain the embarrassing truth, prompting the children to retreat home in shame.
>
> — v5 · CHAPTER XXX. THE GHOST ON THE DYKE

> [Jerry](../character/jerry.md) decrees punishments for the children's cowardice, sending [Carl](../character/carl.md) to sit in the graveyard until midnight. [Carl](../character/carl.md) bravely endures the cold, rainy vigil, but falls dangerously ill with double pneumonia as a result. After a grim fight for his life, [Carl](../character/carl.md) recovers with the support of the family and community, and the children celebrate his return to health.
>
> — v5 · CHAPTER XXXI. CARL DOES PENANCE
